newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mbeki to visit Algeria, Tunisia, Mali.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki to visit Algeria, Tunisia, Mali.

text.p: South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki will visit Algeria, Tunisia and Mali this week to boost trade and develop diplomatic links, the Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
"Discussions will focus on critical African political and economic imperatives," the statement said.

Mbeki, who is almost certain to succeed President Nelson Mandela in 1999, has travelled widely over the past year, visiting Southeast Asia, Europe and North America, as well as several countries in Africa.
The Foreign Ministry noted that Algeria had just completed a multiparty election and Malians were about to go to the polls.
"This visit will manifest South Africa's support for Algerian and Malian democracy," it said.
Mbeki, who will travel with Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad, is also expected to promote economic relations in line with South Africa's policy of expanding trade with African countries.

"Tunisia, Algeria and Mali have considerable untapped mining, agricultural and other resources which, if exploited sustainably, could bring considerably improved quality of life to their people," the statement said.
Mbeki will return to South Africa hours before Mandela leaves on a five-day visit to Britain.
